en.title: Global Wealth Weekly — Cash absorbs record inflows while equity funds attract money despite falling share prices
en.deck: Lipper reports global equity +$38.63bn and money-market +$172.71bn through November 4; ICI US money-market assets reach $8.016tn while gold holdings increase despite lower AUM.
keywords: Lipper global fund flows through Nov4 +38.63bn equity +9.91bn bonds +172.71bn money market, ICI US 8015.74bn asset stock (+114.46)
en.regime: Positive global equity fund subscriptions coexist with large defensive money-market inflows and risky equity price corrections; official credit and currency reserves require slower separate observation.
en.key_risk: Never add overlapping Lipper/ICI universes, interpret AUM as physical holdings, or confuse fund flows with legal change of ownership.

contrary_evidence: Equity fund inflows occur amid declines in equity indices; subscriptions and mark-to-market prices measure different phenomena.
US ICI money-market assets +$114.46bn and worldwide Lipper money-market flow +$172.71bn differ in population and concept.
Gold ETF tonnage +19t with AUM -6% demonstrates holdings versus price valuation.
BIS euro and dollar credit both grow 11% year-over-year; higher euro share is not dollar exit.
limitations: Lipper global sampled fund net flows are not globally comprehensive balance of payments and categories overlap.
ICI US money-market asset changes are stock movements used as proxy for flows, not equal to Lipper global fund flow.
ICI Oct28 combined series is older than Lipper Nov4 and cannot be added.
WGC October physically backed ETF stocks exclude central bank bullion and are priced at changing market levels.
BIS and COFER use Q2 2026 observations, not November flows.
